thread:
maria: heads-up, seeing apiserver 503s + controller-manager leader flips in us-west1 starting ~05:20 UTC, also GPU provisioner backlog growing
ops-bot: ALERT: apiserver_5xx_rate high in cluster-us-west1 (05:22) :rotating_light:
sam: logs?
maria: pasted a few snippets, looks like etcd compaction I/O spikes and probe timeouts
maria: ```
2026-03-20T05:21:54Z apiserver: 503 GET /api/v1/namespaces kube-system 0.123s
2026-03-20T05:22:01Z etcd: compact: finished GC, duration=3456ms iops=1200
2026-03-20T05:22:02Z controller-manager: lost leader lease, renewing
2026-03-20T05:22:05Z provisioner-gpu: attach-queue length=67
```
tera: hmm compaction 3.4s is big, and iops=1200 suggests nvme pressure — any recent snapshot/restore jobs?
maria: ops team ran a nightly snapshot job targeting us-west1 volumes at 05:15 for backups, timing overlaps
julian: link to grafana?
maria: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ctrlplane/etcd-io?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now (chart shows wal_sync and compaction bursts)
sam: also seeing NAT churn on node egress around same time: cloud-nat reassign for gpu-subnet (cloud change) — logs here: ```
Mar 20 05:20:40 node-uw2 kubelet[...]: Network default NAT peer reassign: 10.8.4.0 -> 10.9.0.1
Mar 20 05:21:58 node-uw2 kube-proxy: conntrack: expecting more entries
```
tera: So combined: NVMe snapshot IO + NAT churn -> apiserver watch reconnects -> controller-manager leader hops -> provisioner queues up. Fits.
maria: Current impact: 5-10% of requests 5xx, GPU onboarding slower (90s -> 6m). Customers hitting latency on Dedicated pools.
julian: Ops question: restart controller-manager to stop leader flip? risk making it worse if network still flapping.
sam: don't restart yet. We can: 1) pause snapshot job, 2) throttle compaction/IO, 3) temporarily move GPU warm pool traffic to eu-west1 to reduce customer impact.
maria: pausing snapshot now. ops-bot: runbook step executed: paused backup job us-west1-snapshots by @maria at 05:28 UTC :white_check_mark:
tera: also recommend enabling etcd compaction throttle: set --compaction-interval and lower historical retention for now. I'll open a config PR.
julian: for mitigation, can we add short-lived extra apiserver replicas in us-west1 to absorb watch reconnect storm?
sam: apiserver replicas help only if controlplane nodes healthy; if etcd IO is the bottleneck adding replicas can make it worse. prefer fix IO first.
maria: cost note — tera: if we scale down reserved GPU warm pool during these maintenance windows we save ~ $1.2k/day but onboarding latency jumps. want to propose scheduled window for IO-heavy backups to avoid peak times instead.
julian: +1 to scheduled windows. Customer SLO tradeoffs need ops-lead approval.
tera: PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-config/pull/402 — lowers compaction frequency and adds compaction backoff.
maria: rolling status: paused snapshot (done), NVMe IOPS dropping back to baseline (05:34), provisioner-queue down to 8 (05:36), apiserver 5xx trending to normal (05:38).
ops-bot: RESOLVED: apiserver_5xx_rate alert cleared at 05:40 UTC
maria: follow-ups: schedule backups outside peak, add a pre-check to avoid snapshot on nodes with ongoing high attach ops, and revisit GPU warm-pool cost/runbook choices. I'll open a follow-up ticket and assign to infra-sched.
sam: thx. I'll keep an eye on us-west1 for the next 24h. :thumbsup:
